title: Full-Stack Website Developer
text:
Productsup is a Berlin-based company with a strong international customer base, and we’re looking to rapidly scale our reach within the digital commerce landscape. We are seeking a high-performing Full-Stack Website Developer to join our dynamic Marketing team. In this pivotal role, you will own our website strategy end-to-end, ensuring our site is continuously optimized for conversion and driving performance from foundational back-end architecture to high-impact front-end user experiences.

 Key Responsibilities 
Technical Engineering & Architecture
 
 Back-End (Headless CMS): Design, scale, and maintain Contentful content models, fields, spaces, and environments. Oversee structured content delivery using GraphQL/REST API queries, webhooks, and modern data-handling protocols.

 Front-End (Presentation Layer): Build and maintain responsive, accessible, secure, and performant web experiences using modern JavaScript frameworks (Nuxt.js, Vue.js, Node.js) alongside semantic HTML5 and advanced CSS3.

 Integrations & DevOps: Connect Contentful seamlessly with critical third-party tools, including CRM platforms (HubSpot), web analytics solutions, and cloud infrastructure/hosting environments (AWS, Amazon CloudFront, S3, Heroku).

 AI & Workflow Automation: Enhance, scale, and maintain internal AI-powered automation tools, leveraging platforms such as OpenAI to streamline recurring web workflows, reduce manual operational overhead, and boost overall team efficiency.


Analytics, Tracking & Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)
 
 Performance Monitoring: Evaluate end-to-end site health, user engagement, and marketing funnel performance using GA4, Hotjar, and advanced data visualization tools.

 CRO Pipeline Ownership: Own the testing pipeline by designing (with copy and design support) and executing rigorous A/B and multivariate tests across copy, interactive layouts, and visual CTAs to maximize lead conversion rates.

 Funnel Optimization: Proactively monitor critical site metrics—including Conversion Rate (CVR), bounce rates, and form drop-off trends—to identify conversion friction and engineer immediate solutions.

 Data Integrity & Tagging: Deploy and manage precise event tracking arrays using Google Tag Manager (GTM) and GA4. Conduct thorough QA on all new pages to guarantee exact tag firing, conversion pixel accuracy, and clean UTM parameters.

 Data Flow Architecture: Partner closely with Marketing Operations to secure seamless data flows from web touchpoints into CRMs, data platforms, and executive reporting dashboards.


CMS Enablement, SEO & Support
 
 CMS Training & Enablement: Design and deliver comprehensive CMS onboarding and training sessions for new and existing internal website users.

 Contributor Guidance: Act as the primary technical point of contact for website-related issues, providing continuous documentation, troubleshooting support, and governance for content contributors.

 Publishing Best Practices: Champion best-in-class workflows for web publishing, ensuring content layout consistency, cross-browser compatibility, and digital asset efficiency.

 Technical SEO: Implement foundational and advanced technical SEO requirements in collaboration with the SEO Manager to preserve and improve organic search visibility, site indexation, and page speed performance.



 What You Bring to the Team 
 Technical Background: Proven experience building performant, robust, responsive, and cross-browser compatible Server-Side Rendering (SSR) websites.

 Framework Mastery: Hands-on experience with JavaScript frameworks (specifically Nuxt.js, Vue.js, and Node.js) alongside core HTML5 and CSS3.

 Headless CMS & APIs: Direct experience configuring, managing, and querying headless CMS environments (Contentful strongly preferred), with a fluent understanding of HTTP, JSON, REST, and GraphQL.

 Cloud & DevOps: Competency in managing deployments and environments within cloud services (AWS, S3, Amazon CloudFront), Heroku, and modern version control/project tracking tools (Git, Jira).

 Work Experience: 5+ years of digital operations experience, with at least 1–2 years specifically managing content inside a headless CMS environment.

 Professional Competencies: Strong data-driven mindset, excellent relationship-building skills across design and marketing teams, and the ability to troubleshoot critical bugs under pressure with high autonomy.



 What We Offer You 
 A permanent position with an attractive salary at our growing company

 The option to work remotely and flexibly, because we know outstanding talent knows best how and where to work

 A unique and thorough onboarding program where you’ll learn the ins-and-outs of our company and product

 Ongoing internal and external training, plus a yearly learning budget to help you continuously grow professionally and further your career with Productsup 


 Opportunities for engaging in our Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives, plus one paid Impact Day per year dedicated to voluntary work

 Employee referral bonuses: we know that talent attracts talent, and we encourage you to refer people you know to join our team

 The opportunity to take ownership and responsibility, impacting the company’s growth in an international environment with 40+ nationalities

 Employee Assistance Program



 Productsup values diversity. We celebrate our differences and strive to learn from each other with the firm conviction that diversity drives innovation. Our commitment to equal opportunities begins at the hiring process and extends to our whole working culture. Everyone has a unique contribution to make and all are welcome. About Us

We’ve developed a groundbreaking, vision-powered platform that uses autonomous drones and existing equipment to capture real-time data, completely digitizing workflows that have historically been manual and error-prone. We’re leading the charge in the rapidly evolving robotics industry, and we invite you to join us in reshaping the global supply chain, one intelligent warehouse at a time.
 About the Team 
 You’ll be part of our Engineering organization, working closely with our Full Stack and WMS integration teams. The group builds and operates the production systems behind Gather AI ’s warehouse intelligence platform, including APIs, integrations, data pipelines, databases, and application services used by our customers and internal teams every day.
 This is a small, distributed engineering team where engineers work across a broad technical surface area and have the opportunity to see their work through the full software development lifecycle, from design and development through deployment, production monitoring, troubleshooting, and improvement.
 About the Role 
 We are hiring an SDE II, Full Stack, for our India-based team. You'll build and run the web platforms behind Gather AI 's products - Drone Vision, MHE Vision and SAGE, from the customer-facing dashboards down to the APIs, Integration layers and data pipelines that serve them.
 This is a fully remote, hands-on engineering role for someone early in their career who already has experience building production software and wants broader ownership. You’ll work alongside senior engineers, taking on well-scoped features, integrations, and platform improvements while developing deeper expertise across APIs, backend services, databases, distributed systems, infrastructure, and production reliability.
 You won’t be limited to writing code against someone else’s design. You’ll contribute to technical decisions, troubleshoot systems in production, work through failures and performance issues, and gradually take ownership of components from development through deployment and ongoing support.
 Because our team is distributed across multiple time zones, clear written communication, initiative, and the ability to make progress independently are especially important.
 What You’ll Do 
 
 Build and maintain production backend services using Python and Node.js/NestJS

 Design, build, and maintain REST APIs and integrations with internal and external systems

 Work with PostgreSQL in production, including schema design, complex queries, indexing, connection management, and performance tuning

 Build and support asynchronous workflows using message queues and distributed system patterns

 Apply caching strategies across application and data layers, including understanding cache invalidation and performance tradeoffs

 Take features and integrations through the full software development lifecycle, including development, testing, deployment, monitoring, troubleshooting, and iteration

 Containerize and deploy services using Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines

 Monitor production systems using logs, dashboards, metrics, and other observability tools to understand reliability, throughput, and performance

 Diagnose and resolve production issues, including failures across APIs, integrations, queues, databases, and multi-service workflows

 Contribute to secure development practices including authentication, authorization, secrets handling, and protection against common application vulnerabilities

 Work closely with senior engineers on technical design and architecture decisions while progressively taking greater ownership

 Identify opportunities to improve code, reliability, performance, engineering processes, and system design rather than only executing assigned work

 Collaborate with Engineering, Security, Customer Success, Product, and other teams as our platform continues to scale


 What You’ll Need 
 
 2–5 years of professional software engineering experience building and operating production software

 An engineering degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience

 Production experience with Python and Node.js/NestJS, with strong production depth in at least one and working experience with the other

 Experience building production-grade APIs, microservices, or backend systems and seeing them through deployment and ongoing operation

 Strong SQL fundamentals and hands-on relational database experience, including complex queries, indexing, schema design, and production performance troubleshooting

 Experience designing and maintaining REST APIs, not only consuming them

 Experience integrating with external systems and understanding real-world concerns such as retries, duplicate processing, failure handling, and unreliable dependencies

 Working knowledge of distributed systems concepts including asynchronous processing, message queues, retries, consistency, and failure recovery

 Understanding of caching, including what to cache, where caching should occur, and how invalidation is handled

 Experience with message queues or asynchronous processing technologies such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS, or equivalent

 Experience with Redis or another caching technology

 Experience with Azure or another major cloud provider, deploying and debugging, using Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines

 Familiarity with Git and modern code review workflows

 Understanding of secure coding fundamentals including authentication and authorization, secrets handling, injection risks, and data exposure

 Experience working with production systems beyond simply writing code, including monitoring metrics, investigating performance, responding to failures, and improving systems after issues occur

 Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to document decisions, explain tradeoffs, write clear PRs and design notes, and raise blockers early

 A collaborative and curious approach, with the willingness to contribute ideas, ask questions, accept feedback, and work across component boundaries when needed


 Nice to Have 
 
 Experience building or operating data pipelines, including handling failures, backfills, and data-quality issues

 Familiarity with data engineering concepts such as warehouse or lakehouse modeling, dbt or equivalent, and ETL/ELT design

 Experience with orchestration or streaming technologies such as Airflow, Flink, or similar

 Familiarity with BI and visualization tools such as Metabase, Apache Superset, or equivalent

 Experience with multi-region or geo-distributed systems

 Experience in logistics, warehouse management systems, robotics, or another physical-world technology environment

title: Senior Product Engineer
text:
About Semaphore 

 Semaphore is a remote-first software company building continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) products for engineering teams. Our customers rely on Semaphore Cloud and our self-hosted enterprise products to build, test, and deliver software securely and reliably.
 We have spent years building developer infrastructure at scale. We are now using that foundation to create new products and capabilities for a world in which software is increasingly built by people working with AI coding agents.
 About the role
 We are looking for a senior product engineer who can take an important idea from an early, ambiguous problem to a useful product running in production.
 You will work across product and engineering boundaries: understanding the user, shaping the solution, making technical decisions, building the system, and improving it based on real use. Some work will extend mature Semaphore products. Some will start as a small experiment or a new product. In either case, you will be responsible for getting to a strong outcome, not completing a predefined list of tickets.
 AI coding agents are part of our daily engineering workflow. We expect you to use them fluently to explore, build, test, and ship faster. You remain accountable for the work: choosing the right problem, setting direction, making trade-offs, reviewing what is produced, and ensuring that the result is coherent, reliable, and maintainable.
 This role is for someone with strong ownership, initiative, taste, and judgment. You should be comfortable moving between product questions, system design, code, infrastructure, and user experience as the work requires.
 What you will own
 
 Take product ideas from problem definition through design, implementation, rollout, and iteration, including experiments that may grow into standalone products.

 Work directly with users and internal stakeholders to identify the real problem, decide what is worth building, and make pragmatic scope and architecture decisions.

 Build across backend services, APIs, infrastructure-facing components, and focused frontend experiences, reusing proven Semaphore systems before introducing new infrastructure.

 Use AI coding agents effectively while maintaining a high bar for correctness, security, clarity, and product quality.

 Own the production outcome, including reliability, observability, supportability, and working within Semaphore 's security and compliance requirements. Communicate decisions, progress, and risks clearly.


 What we are looking for
 
 A track record of independently shipping meaningful software products or major product capabilities.

 Strong product judgment: you can identify the essential user problem, reduce unnecessary scope, and recognize when an experience is good enough to ship—or not good enough yet.

 Strong engineering judgment across system design, implementation, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

 Strong backend and systems fundamentals, including APIs, asynchronous processing, service boundaries, state and lifecycle management, retries, idempotency, and failure recovery.

 Comfort with infrastructure concepts such as virtual machines, storage, networking, authentication, secrets, containers, and cloud platforms.

 Ability to navigate a polyglot environment. Semaphore systems include Go, Elixir, Ruby, React, and related technologies; expertise in every language is not required.

 Enough frontend capability to build or extend focused product user experiences without depending on a separate team for every change.

 Fluency with modern AI-assisted development: decomposing work for agents, supplying useful context, reviewing generated changes, and building verification into the workflow.

 Initiative and persistence. You make progress with incomplete information, surface risks early, and bring in other people when their input will improve the result.

 Strong written and spoken English and experience working independently in a remote, asynchronous team.


 We care more about the quality and ownership of what you have built than a specific number of years, previous title, or exact match with our stack.
 Nice to have
 
 Experience building developer tools, CI/CD systems, cloud platforms, or infrastructure products.

 Hands-on experience with distributed systems and event-driven architectures.

 Experience evolving a mature codebase while introducing a new product or architecture alongside it.

 Experience in a lean environment where senior engineers participate directly in product discovery and customer conversations.


 What success looks like
 Within your first three months:
 
 You have taken ownership of a meaningful product problem and shipped a useful capability to production.

 Your work shows good product taste, clear technical decisions, and disciplined scope.

 You have learned enough of Semaphore 's existing platform to reuse its strengths and avoid unnecessary reinvention.

 You are using AI coding agents to increase your output while keeping the resulting systems understandable, tested, and reliable.

 Product and engineering decisions move faster because you bring clear options, make sound calls, and follow through.

 The team trusts you with an ambiguous new product or feature and expects you to drive it to a strong result.


 How you will work
 This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad ownership. You will work closely with engineering, product, infrastructure, and company leadership. Teams are small, communication is direct, and the person closest to the work is expected to exercise judgment.
 You will have room to shape both the product and its implementation. In return, we expect you to take responsibility for the whole outcome: what gets built, why it matters, how well it works, and what happens after it ships.

 Build product features end to end in a modern Next.js and React application — server components, route handlers, client interactivity, and the data layer that connects them.

 We are looking for an experienced and passionate AI-native Software Engineer to join our data science team. This is fundamentally a software engineering role with a strong machine learning focus—we need someone who designs, builds, and operates production systems, and who specializes in the software stack for building and scaling ML models.

 You will take the lead in building the engineering backbone behind our AI-driven bioprocess platform, turning early-stage models into dependable services that our clients and scientists rely on every day. This involves building and operating our portfolio of ML-powered applications, backend services, REST APIs, data pipelines, scheduled jobs, and the dashboards that sit on top of them. Our state-of-the-art ML tools are regularly re-trained on fresh laboratory data to directly shape the decisions our scientists and clients make every week. Your job will be to make sure these systems run reliably, scale gracefully, and evolve cleanly as the science and our client base grow.

 Beyond these core projects, you will collaborate closely with our data scientists, backend engineers, and wet-lab scientists to build Agentic AI systems, manage data pipelines, prepare datasets for machine learning models, and create insightful dashboards to optimize everything from laboratory experiments to commercial-scale manufacturing.

 Key Responsibilities & Workflow 

 
 
 Production ML: Design, develop, and own the production services that power our predictive, optimization, and generative AI applications using FastAPI, PyTorch, and AWS.

 
 MLOps & Infrastructure: Own deployment, retraining workflows, and establish best practices for versioning, CI/CD, observability, and drift monitoring. Be judicious in balancing supporting immediate needs with long-term infrastructure requirements.

 
 Engineering Rigor: Bring modular architecture, typed interfaces, and robust testing to early-stage ML code. Write clean, maintainable, and efficient code, taking ownership of the quality and performance of the ML systems you build.

 
 Backend & Data Connectivity: Create robust REST APIs, ETL pipelines, and human-in-the-loop feedback systems.

 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with data scientists and wet-lab scientists to translate scientific requirements into production constraints.

 
 Agile & AI-Assisted Development: Actively integrate AI-powered tools into your daily workflow to optimize and speed up tasks such as coding, refactoring, testing, and documentation. Effectively use Agile practices to plan and track your work.



 

 Requirements 

 
 
 Education & Experience: Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field from a reputed US/European/APAC University with 2+ years of proven experience as a Full-Stack Developer (or similar role), OR a Bachelor’s degree from a Tier 1 Indian University with 5+ years of experience in a related field.

 
 Frontend Expertise: Deep expertise in building complex, UI-heavy, and responsive web applications using React.js, Next.js, Svelte, etc.

 
 Backend Knowledge: Strong knowledge of Python-based back-end languages such as FastAPI, Django, or similar.

 
 Data & Databases: Experience with databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, or similar, including schema design for experimental or scientific data.

 
 ML in Production: Hands-on experience integrating ML frameworks (PyTorch, Jax, Tensorflow, or similar) into production software, with a clear understanding of how inference, batching, and model lifecycle behave under real load.

 
 Cloud & DevOps: Proven experience deploying and maintaining services and ML models on cloud platforms—AWS (SageMaker, ECS, Lambda), GCP, or similar—alongside proven experience with DevOps practices and CI/CD pipelines.

 
 Core Soft Skills: Strong communication, excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

 The Ideal Candidate & What We Offer

title: Full Stack Product Engineer, Agent Native
text:
About Mactores 

 
 Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most enterprise modernization stalls at pilots and handoffs; ours ships, production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores ' founders' sister company, Aedeon Inc. Aedeon absorbs the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, mapping, validation, test generation, while forward-deployed engineers own architecture, judgment, and cutover. Mactores is Aedeon's flagship deployment partner: field delivery informs the platform roadmap, and the platform shapes how we deliver.
 About Aedeon
 Aedeon is the agent platform for enterprise modernization, built by Aedeon Inc., a separate product company founded by the same team that founded Mactores . Aedeon turns the systems already running a business applications, databases, data platforms, business rules, workflows into governed AI agents, grounded in a persistent Code Intelligence Graph of the customer's own code and verified through behavior-equivalence proof. Aedeon is delivered as a product, not a services engagement, and runs without mandatory forward-deployed engineers. 
 This role puts you inside the platform side of that loop: you'll ship product features on Aedeon itself. Aedeon is the agent-native modernization platform for the enterprise, it turns the systems already running the business (applications, databases, data platforms, business rules, workflows) into governed AI agents, grounded in a persistent Code Intelligence Graph of the customer's own code and verified through behavior-equivalence proof. Aedeon is delivered as a product, not a services engagement, and runs without mandatory forward-deployed engineers. It has real enterprise customers and tight release timelines.
 We're looking for a senior full-stack developer who is deeply product-oriented, takes release ownership seriously, and brings a rigorous, test-first mindset to every feature they ship. You understand the full delivery lifecycle, building features, defining test cases, running deployments, validating production readiness and you use AI agents and automation to do it at a high standard of quality and efficiency. Agents don't replace your judgment here; they multiply it. You'll use AI tooling to generate test coverage at scale, and you'll own the calls the tooling can't make.
 We're not looking for someone who builds features and hands them off. We're looking for someone who ships features they'd be proud to demo, loses sleep over a broken deployment and fixes it before anyone asks, writes test cases before the code rather than after the deadline, uses every tool available including AI to work better and faster, and treats the release date as a promise to the team and the customer. You think like a product owner: quality, timelines, and the end-user experience are personal responsibilities. You commit to release deadlines and raise risks early enough to do something about them.
 What will you do
 
 Product development

 Design, build, and maintain full-stack features across the Aedeon frontend (React + Next.js) with a focus on reliability, performance, and user experience.

 Work with product management, designers, and backend/DevOps engineers to take features from requirement to deployed, tested release.

 Participate actively in sprint planning, backlog grooming, and retrospectives with a product-first perspective.

 Release ownership

 Own delivery of your features end to end — development through deployment and post-release validation.

 Commit to sprint and release deadlines and hit them. Flag blockers and risks with enough lead time to mitigate them.

 Coordinate with DevOps and QA so the deployment pipeline is ready and the release process is clean and repeatable.

 Testing and quality

 Practice test-driven development. The test defines what "done" means before the code ships.

 Write detailed, accurate test cases for every feature before deployment — functional flows, edge cases, regression scenarios, integration touchpoints.

 Use AI-assisted tools to generate high-quality test cases at scale and validate them for coverage completeness.

 Build and maintain automated test suites (E2E, integration, unit) and integrate them into the CI/CD pipeline.

 Run thorough deployment validations in staging before any production release. No feature ships without sign-off.

 Collaboration and documentation

 Write clear, maintainable code with adequate documentation. Review pull requests thoroughly and give constructive feedback.

 Document APIs, deployment procedures, test plans, and architectural decisions in Confluence or equivalent tools.

 Share testing best practices with the team and hold the line on quality and release discipline.


 What you need for this opportunity
 
 Frontend

 Strong proficiency in React.js: component architecture, state management, hooks, and performance optimization.

 Strong proficiency in the Next.js framework.

 Experience building real-time interfaces using WebSocket APIs.

 Proficiency in TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and modern frontend tooling (Vite, Webpack).

 Experience implementing OAuth 2.0 flows (GitHub OAuth, AWS Cognito) in the frontend.

 Familiarity with responsive design and cross-browser compatibility.

 Cloud and infrastructure

 Working knowledge of AWS services: S3, DynamoDB, SES, Cognito, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch.

 Comfort navigating multi-account AWS environments (dev/uat/prod) and an understanding of VPC networking basics.

 Testing and automation

 Test-driven development as a discipline. Tests written before the code, not after.

 Hands-on experience writing and maintaining automated test suites: E2E (Playwright or Cypress), integration tests, and unit tests.

 Experience using AI tools (Claude, LLM-based test generators) to accelerate and improve test case quality.

 Ability to write structured, accurate test cases from product requirements: functional, edge case, regression, and integration coverage.

 Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.


 You'll be preferred if you have
 
 Knowledge of Amazon OpenSearch Service or Elasticsearch.

 Experience with RabbitMQ or other message queue systems.

 Prior work on B2B SaaS products with a structured release process.


 How we work?
 
 Mactores was built agent-native from day one: agents absorb the repetitive 60–70% of delivery work, and engineers own the judgment. The same logic applies inside this role AI tooling generates test coverage and accelerates the routine work, and you own architecture, release calls, and the promise behind the date. Because Mactores ' founders also founded Aedeon Inc., field delivery and platform development feed each other: what our forward-deployed engineers learn on customer engagements shapes what gets built, and what you build shapes what ships for customers. 

 Life at Mactores 

 We care about creating a culture that makes a real difference in the lives of every Mactorian. Our 10 Core Leadership Principles that honor Decision-making, Leadership, Collaboration, and Curiosity drive how we work.
 1. Be one step ahead
 2. Deliver the best
 3. Be bold
 4. Pay attention to the detail
 5. Enjoy the challenge
 6. Be curious and take action
 7. Take leadership
 8. Own it
 9. Deliver value
 10. Be collaborative
 We would like you to read more details about the work culture on 
 
 The Path to Joining the Mactores Team 
 At Mactores , our recruitment process is built around distinct structured stages. Here's an overview of what to expect at each stage:


 
 Take-home Assessment:

 A technical task relevant to the role, so you can demonstrate your thinking and approach at your own pace. 

 Technical Interview:A hands-on session with one of our panel members covering your technical skills, hands-on experience, and how you deliver quality under pressure. 
 Panel Interview: 
A structured conversation with members of the hiring team covering your experience, product thinking, and how you work. 

 HR Discussion: During this 30-minute session, you'll have the opportunity to discuss the offer and next steps with a member of the HR team. 

 At Mactores , we are committed to providing equal opportunities in all of our employment practices, and we do not discriminate based on race, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, marital status, military status, genetic information, or any other category protected by federal, state, and local laws. This policy extends to all aspects of the employment relationship, including recruitment, compensation, promotions, transfers, disciplinary action, layoff, training, and social and recreational programs. All employment decisions will be made in compliance with these principles.

title: Senior Front-End Engineer
text:
Senior Frontend Engineer
 About Inco
 Inco is building the confidentiality layer for blockchains through encryption technologies. We’re building the next generation of secure, scalable, and privacy-enhancing solutions for Web3, enabling fintech, payments, and blockchain applications to have the same confidentiality and capabilities users expect from Web2.
 Who You Are
 We’re looking for a senior frontend engineer who has built production-grade Web3 user experiences and understands the unique complexity of blockchain applications.
 You have strong frontend fundamentals, but you also understand that Web3 frontend engineering is not just about building interfaces. It requires safely fetching and interpreting onchain data, integrating wallets, handling signatures, managing client-side state, and designing user flows where security and correctness matter.
 You should be comfortable building polished, reliable UIs while also thinking deeply about how users interact with wallets, sign messages, grant permissions, manage session keys, and execute intent-based flows. You understand the security risks of asking users to sign transactions or messages, and you care about making those flows clear, safe, and difficult to misuse.
 We’re looking for someone senior who can own frontend architecture end-to-end, raise engineering standards, and mentor more junior engineers. You should be the type of person who can turn ambiguous product requirements into secure, elegant, production-ready user experiences.
 This role is remote / hybrid / based in Bangalore (preferred).
 Responsibilities
 Frontend Architecture & Development
 
 Design, build, and maintain production-grade frontend applications using modern frontend technologies.

 Own frontend features end-to-end, from product requirements and UX flows to implementation, testing, and deployment.

 Build responsive, performant, and reliable user interfaces for Web3 products.

 Create reusable frontend components, patterns, and architecture that allow the team to move quickly without sacrificing quality.

 Work closely with product, design, backend, and protocol teams to translate complex Web3 flows into intuitive user experiences.


 Web3 Product & Wallet Integration
 
 Build frontend experiences that integrate with wallets, smart contracts, indexers, RPC providers, and blockchain data sources.

 Implement flows involving transaction signing, message signing, intent signing, session keys, delegated permissions, and account abstraction.

 Design user experiences around balances, transaction history, onchain transactions, permissions, and Web3 payment flows.

 Understand how to fetch, cache, reconcile, and display onchain and offchain data safely and accurately.

 Handle edge cases common in Web3 applications, including pending transactions, reorgs, failed RPC calls, wallet disconnects, chain switching, stale balances, and inconsistent indexer data.


 Security & Correctness
 
 Ensure frontend flows are secure by default, especially when users are asked to sign messages, authorize intents, or store session keys locally.

 Apply best practices for client-side key management, session key storage, permission scoping, signature domain separation, and phishing-resistant UX.

 Work with the team to identify and prevent risks around malicious signatures, replay attacks, unsafe approvals, incorrect transaction previews, and confusing wallet prompts.

 Treat frontend correctness as critical infrastructure, especially when user funds or private information are involved.


 Leadership & Mentorship
 
 Lead technical design discussions and help define frontend architecture, standards, and best practices.

 Review code and mentor junior engineers on frontend quality, Web3 security, testing, and production readiness.

 Improve engineering velocity by building strong abstractions, documentation, and internal tooling.

 Take ownership of frontend quality across performance, reliability, security, accessibility, and maintainability.


 Required Experience
 
 5+ years of frontend engineering experience, with strong production experience building complex applications.

 Strong expertise in TypeScript, React, and modern frontend development.

 Experience building Web3, crypto, wallet, DeFi, payments, or blockchain-related frontend products.

 Strong understanding of wallet integrations, transaction flows, message signing, and onchain data fetching.

 Experience working with libraries and tools such as viem, wagmi, ethers.js, WalletConnect, RainbowKit, or similar.

 Strong understanding of frontend state management, API integration, caching, and real-time data updates.

 Ability to reason carefully about security-sensitive frontend flows involving user funds, permissions, signatures, or keys.

 Experience owning large frontend features from design to production.

 Strong communication skills and ability to work closely with product, design, backend, and protocol engineers.

 Experience mentoring junior engineers and raising frontend engineering standards.

 Startup mindset: comfortable with ambiguity, fast iteration, and taking ownership end-to-end.


 Preferred Qualifications
 
 Experience building wallets, smart account interfaces, account abstraction flows, or session key systems.

 Experience with intent-based protocols, delegated permissions, EIP-712 signatures, EIP-1271, EIP-4337, or EIP-7702.

 Experience building frontend interfaces for privacy-preserving, security-sensitive, or financial applications.

 Experience with indexers, subgraphs, custom backend APIs, RPC providers, and blockchain event reconciliation.

 Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex Web3 flows for mainstream users.

 Experience with frontend testing, including unit tests, integration tests, end-to-end tests, and wallet interaction testing.

 Experience with Next.js, Tailwind, design systems, component libraries, and frontend performance optimization.

 Open-source contributions or prior work in crypto, wallets, DeFi, payments, or developer tools.


 What Success Looks Like
 
 You will help build the frontend experience for Inco’s core products, making advanced privacy and Web3 payment flows feel simple, secure, and intuitive.

 You will be responsible for creating interfaces that users can trust when signing intents, managing permissions, interacting with wallets, and moving funds privately.

 You will help establish the frontend foundation for Inco’s products while mentoring the team and setting a high bar for quality, security, and user experience.

title: Senior Mobile Platform Engineer
text:
Proudly recognized as a Great Place to Work®, we are an AI-native customer experience platform purpose-built for emerging markets.  Our Engineering team is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining the systems and technologies that drive Unifonic ’s solutions. We work closely with other departments to ensure our products and services meet the needs of our customers. If you are passionate about technology and are excited about working on cutting-edge communication and engagement solutions, we want you on our team.
 As a Mobile Platform Engineer, you’ll own our SDK platform end to end—treating it like a product that developers rely on every day. You’ll shape the foundations that make our mobile experiences reliable, extensible, and easy to integrate.
 Your week will span the full platform lifecycle: roughly a third of your time will go into the shells, packaging, and add-ons that bring the SDK to life; about a fifth will focus on the core SDK and the contracts that keep it stable and predictable. The rest will take you across customer troubleshooting, release engineering, documentation, and exploring new platform capabilities.

 Designing the public API of the SDK on your primary platform and keep it idiomatic: async and AsyncSequence on iOS, suspend and Flow on Android, Promises and events on the web.


 Writing the contract for each feature by hand: new event and command variants in the core, the public API shape, and the conformance vectors that every shell must pass.


 Implementing features in the Rust core and the shell executors, with coding agents doing much of the typing and you owning every line that merges.


 Translating OS lifecycle into SDK behavior: scene phases, process death, background limits, push wake-ups, connectivity changes, app extensions.


 Building and keeping green the release pipeline: one coordinated release produces the XCFramework, AAR, npm packages and sample apps, signed, with symbols, SBOM and privacy manifest.


 Running the consumer test matrix: tiny storefront apps per configuration (minimum Xcode and AGP, R8 full mode, arm64-only ABI filters, React Native new architecture, Expo prebuild, Vite, webpack, ).


 Handling merchant tickets on rotation: triage by layer, replay diagnostics bundles, fix with a new vector or platform test, ship a patch release.


 Shipping platform-specific add-ons beside the common SDK: rich push with product images, in-app campaign UI, Android Binder service, FCM forwarding, App Attest and Play Integrity.


 Keeping the observability contract: structured logs with correlation ids, metrics callbacks, stable error codes, diagnostics() and selfCheck() .


 Tracking annual OS, Xcode, AGP and React Native changes and land them before merchants hit them.


 Writing what you decide: ADRs, changelogs, migration notes and integration docs that a person or a coding agent can follow to a first tracked event in under 30 minutes.

 What you'll bring:
 
 7+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years working on a library, SDK, framework, or platform consumed by third-party developers.


 Strong experience with public API design and Semantic Versioning (SemVer), including managing deprecations without breaking existing customers.


 Deep understanding of mobile platform lifecycles, including process death and restoration, background execution limits, push wake-ups, extensions, and platform services.


 Hands-on experience with native build systems and packaging, including publishing to a package registry and troubleshooting third-party builds.


 Experience with FFI and language interoperability, such as JNI/NDK on Android, C interoperability with Swift, or another production-shipped language boundary.


 Experience supporting third-party integrators through documentation, technical support, troubleshooting, and analyzing symbolicated crash reports.


 Strong testing mindset, using tests as a design tool rather than simply a validation step; experience with property-based or mutation testing is a plus.

 Android

 Experience with consumer ProGuard/R8 rules and JNI/NDK, including native library packaging across ABIs.


 Production experience with Android lifecycle and background execution, including process death, Doze, background restrictions, and WorkManager.


 Strong TypeScript experience, including at least one published npm package.


 Experience building React Native native modules using the New Architecture.

 Hands-on experience with Claude Code , including skill files, commands, and structured prompts.

 Mobile SDK & Library Development

 iOS & Android Platform Expertise

title: Software Development Engineer II (Frontend) - Opportunities
text:
About HighLevel : HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

 Our people 
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

 Our impact 
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts 

 
 About the Role: 

 
 We are looking for an SDE-2 Frontend-leaning Full-Stack Engineer to build the interface of CRM Opportunities, the deal and pipeline engine at the heart of our CRM. Opportunities is the system of record for every revenue motion our customers run, from lead conversion to closed-won, and the pipeline board is where our customers spend their working day. 

 This role is frontend-first. The hard problems here are interface problems: a drag-and-drop pipeline board that stays smooth with thousands of cards on screen, optimistic updates that roll back cleanly when a write fails, deal detail views assembled from arbitrary customer-defined custom fields, filters and saved views that hold up under real use, and keeping all of it coherent as several people move deals in the same pipeline at once. Getting this right is the difference between a CRM customers tolerate and one they trust. 

 You will own frontend features end-to-end in Vue.js, and you will go into the backend as the work requires — extending an API, shaping a response so the client does not have to over-fetch, adding an endpoint that serves the view you are building. You do not need to be a backend specialist; you do need to be unafraid of the server side and happy to work in it rather than filing a ticket. Senior engineers own the broader architecture and are there for design guidance and review. 





 What You Will Do: 

 
 
 Own frontend features across Opportunities in Vue.js — the pipeline board, deal detail views, stage and pipeline configuration, filters and saved views, bulk actions, and reporting surfaces


 Build interactions that have to feel instant: drag-and-drop stage moves, inline edits, optimistic updates with clean rollback and clear error states when a write fails


 Make large pipelines fast in the browser — virtualized and windowed lists, pagination and lazy loading, render and re-render cost, bundle size, and time to first meaningful paint on a board with thousands of deals


 Design and maintain client-side state and data-fetching patterns (Pinia/Vuex, caching, invalidation) so the UI stays consistent without redundant round-trips


 Handle concurrency in the interface: live updates when a teammate moves a deal, stale-data detection, and sensible conflict resolution


 Render dynamic, customer-defined schemas — custom fields, custom objects, and per-workspace configuration — without special-casing every variation


 Build reusable, well-composed components, and contribute to the shared design system rather than growing one-off UI


 Work directly from designs, and push back with product and design where an interaction will not hold up in practice


 Extend the backend where your feature needs it: adding or reshaping NestJS API endpoints, trimming over-fetching, and adjusting payloads for the view you are building


 Write tests that matter — component and unit tests, plus end-to-end coverage of the flows customers cannot afford to have broken


 Instrument the frontend: error tracking, real-user performance monitoring, and the event data needed to see how a feature is actually used


 Care about accessibility, keyboard support, responsive layout, and cross-browser behavior as part of shipping, not as a follow-up


 Take part in on-call for the surfaces you own, debug production issues, and contribute to postmortems


 Write clear design docs for the features you own, and participate actively in design and code review



 


 What You will Need: 

 
 3+ years building and shipping production frontend applications 


 Strong JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals, and depth in a component framework — Vue preferred, React fine if you are willing to work in Vue 


 Real experience with complex, stateful interfaces — not just forms and CRUD screens 


 Practical grasp of frontend performance: rendering cost, long lists, network waterfalls, bundle size, and how to profile rather than guess 


 Comfortable consuming and debugging REST APIs, and confident enough in a backend codebase (Node.js/NestJS or similar) to make the change your feature needs 


 Solid CSS and layout skills, and an eye for whether a build matches the design 


 Experience shipping and supporting features you wrote — design through deploy 


 Comfort working with a degree of ambiguity, asking good questions, and driving a task to done 






 Preferred Qualifications: 

 
 Built a board, kanban, table, grid, or calendar interface with drag-and-drop and large data volumes 


 Exposure to CRM, sales, pipeline, or workflow products 


 Experience with dynamic or schema-driven UI — rendering interfaces from customer-defined configuration 


 Worked on real-time or collaborative interfaces (WebSockets, polling, optimistic concurrency) 


 Experience with multi-tenant SaaS, including white-labelled or themeable products 


 Familiarity with Vue 3, Pinia, Vite, and end-to-end testing (Playwright or Cypress) 


 Backend experience with Node.js/NestJS and MongoDB 


 Product instincts and a portfolio or GitHub of shipped work — we will want to look at interfaces you have built 





 Tech Skill Set: 

 Vue.js (Vue 3, Pinia, Vite), TypeScript, modern CSS — backed by Node.js (NestJS) APIs, MongoDB, and Redis, running on a distributed microservices architecture over Istio service mesh. 


 What Success Looks Like: 

 
 Ships Opportunities frontend features to production reliably, with steadily less guidance over time 


 Builds interfaces that stay fast and predictable as workspaces grow from hundreds to millions of deals 


 Turns fiddly interaction problems into implementations that hold up in real customer use, not just in a demo 


 Leaves the component layer better composed and more reusable than they found it 


 Makes the backend change their feature needs instead of waiting on someone else 


 Debugs production issues independently and leaves behind better instrumentation than they found 


 Grows into owning larger, more ambiguous pieces of the product

Everis has a different standard for talent. We do not use years of experience, titles, or pedigree as substitutes for ability. We look for exceptional work, sound judgment, fast learning, ownership, and evidence of impact. It is not a lower bar. It is a sharper one.
 We’re looking for an accomplished software engineer who has built real mobile applications and already has practical exposure to growth, experimentation, conversion optimization, or broader product work. This role requires both engineering depth and evidence that you can think beyond implementation. 
 Join Everis at a defining stage of growth. Help shape the product, influence the company we become, and grow with us. Work 100% remotely from anywhere, benefit from unlimited leave, and connect with colleagues at company-sponsored international retreats in some of the world’s most inspiring cities.
 About Everis 
 Everis is a growing, remote-first software company founded by proven technology entrepreneurs Rob Rawson and Liam Martin, who previously built Time Doctor into an eight-figure global SaaS business. We acquire promising mobile apps and SaaS companies, invest in their future, and improve their products, technology, and customer experience. Our ambition is to make Everis the best long-term home for exceptional software products—and a company where exceptional people can take real ownership, do consequential work, and grow with us.
 About the Product 
 Pebble is Everis ’s growing, speaking-first language-learning app for iOS and Android. It helps people learn English, Spanish, and French through practical lessons, pronunciation practice, and guided conversations that get them speaking from day one. The product is live and evolving quickly, with major opportunities across onboarding, habit formation, activation, retention, conversion, and new markets. Your engineering and product decisions will directly influence how well people learn and how quickly Pebble grows.
 What makes this role different 
 Most engineering roles begin after the problem, solution, and ticket have already been defined. Here, you join the work earlier. You will remain a software engineer first, but you will also identify product problems, decide what to test, build the solution, measure the outcome, and use the evidence to determine what happens next. This is not a marketing role for someone who codes; it is an engineering role with responsibility for product outcomes.
 What you’ll work on 
 
 Build, ship, and improve Pebble’s mobile applications.


 Find friction across onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, conversion, and monetization.


 Turn product questions into improvements, prototypes, A/B tests, and other useful experiments.


 Use product and user data to understand behavior and decide what should be built next.


 Define success measures, analyze results, and act on what you learn.


 Work directly with our founders and product and business leadership.


 Balance strong engineering with the speed required to test ideas and learn.



 What you need to bring 
 This is a mobile engineering job first. You need to have built, shipped, and supported a production mobile app. We mean a real product used by real people - not just a demo or code sample.
 We also need proof you've thought beyond implementation. Show us at least one of these:
 
 Breadth beyond implementation. Direct mobile-growth or conversion work You must show meaningful evidence of at least one of the following: growth experimentation, A/B or split testing, conversion optimization, product ownership, building and operating your own software product.


 Conversion optimization. You improved a real flow: onboarding, activation, a paywall, trial-to-paid, checkout, or another point where users dropped.


 Core Stack. Strong engineering fundamentals and sound judgment about reliability, maintainability, quality, and speed. Flutter/Dart, TypeScript/NestJS, MongoDB, or close equivalents; and App Store or Google Play subscriptions, paywalls, payments, or trial-to-paid journeys.


 Production mobile engineering. Demonstrated success building and shipping production mobile applications using iOS, Android, cross-platform, or another credible mobile environment.


 Product development or ownership. You helped decide what to build and why. You didn't just receive a finished specification. You can independently take production software from problem through implementation, release, and iteration.


 Product-management-type work. You framed the problem, made trade-offs, defined success, or used evidence to choose the next move.


 A product of your own. You built it, launched it, watched real people use it, and changed it based on what you learned.



 What good looks like 
 
 Your fundamentals are solid. APIs, data modelling, testing, debugging, release practices, and production monitoring aren't someone else's job.


 You can tell the whole story. What was wrong, what you personally built, what happened, and what you did next.


 You cross boundaries when the problem demands it. Mobile, backend, web, data, analytics - you don't stop at the edge of your code.


 You'd rather find out than argue from theory. You form a view, test it, and change your mind when the evidence says you should.

 Consequential ownership: your decisions will directly affect Pebble and Everis .


 Direct founder access: work closely with experienced entrepreneurs on important product and company decisions.

 About the Role: 
 
 We are seeking an SDE-3 Backend Builder to own the CRM Opportunities product end-to-end. Opportunities is the deal and pipeline engine at the heart of our CRM — the system of record for every revenue motion our customers run, from lead conversion to closed-won. 

 This role emphasises deep backend ownership: designing data models, APIs, and distributed workflows that power pipelines, stages, automations, reporting, and integrations at scale. You will operate with high autonomy, turning ambiguous problems into production systems, with enough frontend fluency to ship the occasional UI surface without waiting on anyone. 

 Opportunities is also where a growing set of AI-assisted features live — things like surfacing what needs attention in a pipeline, summarising deal context, and suggesting next steps. To be clear about the shape of that work: we are not training or serving models. These features are built on top of existing AI capabilities, and the engineering problem is the product plumbing around them — assembling the right context from CRM data, keeping latency and cost sane, handling failure and non-deterministic output gracefully, and making the results trustworthy enough for a customer to act on. You do not need an ML background; you need the judgement to build a reliable product feature on top of a probabilistic dependency.

 Own the full lifecycle of the Opportunities backend: translate business and customer needs into scalable, production-grade services 

 Design and evolve the data model for pipelines, stages, deals, and associated entities — getting consistency, throughput, and query patterns right 

 Build and scale APIs, event-driven workflows, and background jobs that handle high-volume writes, automations, and integrations 

 Tackle distributed systems concerns: idempotency, eventual consistency, race conditions, hot tenants, and noisy-neighbor isolation 

 Improve performance and reliability of large pipelines (millions of opportunities per workspace) through indexing, sharding, caching, and query optimization 

 Build the AI-assisted surfaces of Opportunities on top of existing AI capabilities — context assembly from CRM data, prompt and response contracts, caching, cost and latency budgets, graceful degradation when a call is slow, wrong, or unavailable, and a feedback loop for measuring output quality 

 Ship end-to-end when needed — including UI changes in Vue — without blocking on cross-functional handoffs 

 Instrument the system: logs, metrics, traces, and SLOs that make production behavior legible 

 Drive incident response, postmortems, and the engineering hygiene that keeps a high-traffic product healthy 


 What you will need: 
 
 4+ years building and operating production backend systems at scale 

 Strong fundamentals in data modeling (SQL and NoSQL), API design, and distributed systems 

 Hands-on experience with Node.js or Go in production 

 Track record of owning services end-to-end — design, build, deploy, on-call 

 Comfort working independently in ambiguous problem spaces with high ownership 

 Solid grasp of scalability, performance, and reliability trade-offs 


 Preferred Qualifications: 
 
 Experience building CRM, sales, pipeline, or workflow products 

 Worked on multi-tenant SaaS at scale (sharding, tenant isolation, fair-use limits) 

 Familiarity with event streaming (Kafka/Redis Streams), queues, and async processing 

 Exposure to MongoDB, Postgres, ElasticSearch, ClickHouse, or similar at non-trivial scale 

 Have shipped a customer-facing feature backed by an LLM or similar AI API — and have opinions on where it worked and where it did not. No modelling or ML-infrastructure background required 

 Frontend fluency in Vue.js — enough to ship a feature without a frontend partner 

 Strong product instincts and a portfolio or GitHub of shipped work

 Node.js (NestJS), Go, Vue.js, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka / Pub-Sub, ElasticSearch — running on a distributed microservices architecture over Istio service mesh, with AI-assisted features built on top of existing AI/LLM APIs. 

 What Success Looks Like:

 Builds services that stay reliable as workspaces grow from thousands to millions of deals

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

 What Will You Build 
 
 Build and ship native Android features for onboarding, accounts, cards, payments, transfers, rewards and AI-assisted user journeys.

title: Product Engineer (Contract)
text:
There is a working product. There is one founder. There is no team yet.
 The product needs someone to take it the rest of the way — finish the build, harden it, test it, put it in front of the first real users, and stay close enough to those users to know what to fix next.
 That's the job. It is not a well-defined ticket queue. It's closer to: here is the thing, here is what "done" means, go. 
 This is a paid contract role. We're paying for your time and your expertise, and we expect to pay properly for both.
 What we're building
 An orchestration layer that sits above the frontier AI models — Claude, GPT, Gemini — and coordinates them rather than picking one.
 It is aimed at people whose work product is judgment, where being wrong is expensive and "the AI said so" is not an acceptable answer.
 Where things actually stand
 
 The core product works end to end.

 There's a real documentation and decision-log discipline in place — architecture invariants, contracts, a decision record going back months, git hooks enforcing some of it. You will not be reverse-engineering a mystery.

 There are known open bugs, known unfinished surfaces, and a UI that needs an aesthetics pass.

 It has never had a user who wasn't the founder.


 The gap between "works" and "someone else can use this without me sitting next to them" is the gap you're being hired to close.
 What you'd own
 Phase 1 — Close it out (first weeks)
 
 Finish the remaining feature work; hide or cut what isn't ready

 Aesthetics and UX pass — it needs to feel like a product, not a prototype

 Fix the open bug list; expand test coverage

 Security hardening pass ahead of real users (external review budgeted separately — you'll work with it, not carry it alone)


 Phase 2 — Alpha
 
 Ship it to real users

 Onboarding: get people from signup to first genuine use without hand-holding

 Support them directly. You'll be answering the emails. This is a feature of the job, not a chore attached to it.

 Instrument it enough to know what people actually do, versus what they say they do


 Phase 3 — Beta and beyond
 
 Turn alpha behaviour into the beta roadmap

 Help make the call on who this ships to first: individual professionals, small firms, or enterprise

 Build the systems and documentation that let a bigger team pick this up later


 Stack
 
 Frontend: vanilla JS, HTML, CSS — a single-file monolith, no framework. Deliberate. It'll be broken up when there's a reason, not before.

 Backend: Supabase (Postgres, auth, storage)

 Hosting: Netlify, deploy on push

 Provider APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google

 Node for tooling and tests


 If you need a framework to be effective, this isn't your project. If reading 5,000 lines of someone else's JavaScript and immediately knowing where the bodies are buried sounds fine, keep reading.
 Who we're looking for
 Someone who uses both sides of their brain.
 One side reads code carefully. Spots the branch that swallows an error without telling anyone. Doesn't trust a function just because of its name. Can hold the whole system in their head and work out what a change will break three files away.
 The other side thinks about the person on the other side of the screen. Why they gave up at step three. Which feature they'll ask for and never use. What would make them tell a colleague about this.
 Most people are good at one. We want someone who is genuinely strong on the code side and has real instinct for the user side — someone who can look at a screen and say "this works, and nobody will use it," and be right.
 Hard requirement: you have shipped something real inside an agentic coding harness. 
 We mean you have worked inside Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider, or something equivalent — as your main development environment — and something you built that way exists, runs, and has been used by someone other than you. You know how these tools fail. You know what they'll confidently get wrong. You've built your own habits around checking what they produce, because you've been burned by not doing it.
 Using AI to look things up or to explain code is not the same thing, and isn't what we're asking about.
 And you finish things. One small project that shipped, got users, and was supported for months tells us more than ten impressive repos that stopped at 80%. We're being direct about this because the failure mode of this role is a beautiful, elaborate, unlaunched product.
 What we are not asking for
 
 A degree, or a degree in progress, or a degree completed

 A specific number of years. Second-year student and twenty-five-year veteran are both entirely welcome, and will be assessed identically.

 A recognisable logo on your CV

 Deep security or infrastructure specialisation — that's brought in as expertise where it's needed

 Prior startup experience


 The founder covers strategy, product direction, positioning, and go-to-market. What's missing is build capacity and someone who owns getting it in front of users.
 Hard requirement: you've shipped something real inside an agentic harness — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider. As your actual dev environment, not as a lookup tool. And someone other than you has used what you built.
 Don't care about your degree, your years, or your logos. Student or twenty-year veteran, same bar.
 Stack: vanilla JS single-file monolith, Supabase, Netlify. No framework. If that sounds fine, we should talk.
 Full-time, 40 hours a week, remote, with overlap into US morning or evening hours. Two months to start, with the possibility to continue.
 To apply, send me one thing you shipped with an agentic harness, whether anyone else ever used it, and — in five lines — the first three things you'd do with a working product and zero users.
 Send an email with:
 
 One thing you shipped using an agentic coding harness. Link to it, live if possible. Tell us which harness, what it got wrong, and how you caught it.


 Whether anyone other than you ever used it — how many people, for how long, and what broke when they did.


 Five lines, no more: you've just been handed a working product with zero users. What are the first three things you do?


 One thing you've killed. A feature, a project, an approach you'd invested real time in and cut anyway. Why.


 No cover letter. No CV unless you want to send one. We're reading for judgment, not formatting.
 Shortlisted candidates get a full walkthrough of what's been built, followed by a coding interview.
 Terms
 
 
 Engagement: Contract

 
 Commitment: Full-time, 40 hours per week

 
 Duration: 2 months, starting immediately, with the possibility to continue

 
 Location: Remote. Overlap with US morning and/or evening hours required.


 This is for a US start up.

title: Machine Learning Software Engineer II
text:
Cambium Learning® Group is an award-winning educational technology solutions leader dedicated to helping all students reach their potential through individualized and differentiated instruction. Using a research-based, personalized approach, Cambium Learning Group delivers SaaS resources and instructional products that engage students and support teachers in fun, positive, safe and scalable environments. These solutions are provided through Learning A-Z® (online differentiated instruction for elementary school reading, writing and science), ExploreLearning® (online interactive math and science simulations, a math fact fluency solution, and a K–2 science solution), Voyager Sopris Learning® (blended solutions that accelerate struggling learners to achieve in literacy and math and professional development for teachers), and VKidz Learning (online comprehensive homeschool education and programs for literacy and science). We believe that every student has unlimited potential, that teachers matter, and that data, instruction, and practice are the keys to success in the classroom and beyond.
 Job Overview:
 We are seeking a talented Machine Learning Engineer II to join our CAI machine learning and scoring development team. In this role, you will be the crucial bridge between applied research and production systems. Working alongside a cross‑functional group of mathematicians, computer scientists, psychometricians, and statisticians, you will design and deploy custom machine learning solutions for our clients and internal platforms.
 The ideal candidate is a full‑stack ML practitioner who is equally comfortable discussing algorithmic design with researchers and architecting scalable, low‑latency production systems. You will own the full software development lifecycle—transforming research prototypes into optimized, production‑ready solutions using modern AWS infrastructure such as SageMaker, ECS, and Lambda, with an emphasis on high‑throughput inference and PyTorch‑to‑ONNX model optimization.
 Job Responsibilities:
 
 
 Full-Lifecycle ML Development: Lead the transition of machine learning models from theoretical prototypes into scalable, high-performance production systems.

 
 AWS Cloud Architecture & Deployment: Architect and deploy ML solutions utilizing AWS ECS (Elastic Container Service) for containerized workloads and AWS Lambda for serverless, event-driven inference pipelines.

 
 Model & Inference Optimization: Optimize PyTorch models for production deployment by converting them to ONNX formats. Apply advanced inference optimization techniques (quantization, pruning, ONNX Runtime) and memory-efficient attention mechanisms like Flash Attention to minimize latency and maximize throughput.

 
 Infrastructure & Engineering Best Practices: Champion infrastructure best practices for machine learning systems, establishing reliable CI/CD pipelines, and ensuring robust, secure, and reproducible deployments across the AWS ecosystem.

 
 Algorithm Engineering: Design, develop, and evaluate algorithms that generate descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive insights from both structured and unstructured data.

 
 Robust Software Engineering: Write clean, efficient, and well-tested code. Complete rigorous testing, debugging, and documentation to ensure seamless installation and long-term maintenance.

 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Actively participate in research discussions, requirements gathering, and system design alongside domain experts to build tailored scoring and ML solutions.


 Job Requirements:
 
 
 Experience: 2–5 years of industry experience in Machine Learning Engineering, Software Engineering, or Data Science, with a proven track record of architecting and deploying models to production.

 
 Cloud & MLOps Infrastructure: Deep, hands-on experience with the AWS ecosystem, specifically AWS ECS and Lambda . Solid understanding of containerization (Docker) and event-driven architectures.

 
 Programming Proficiency: Strong proficiency in modern programming languages used in ML (e.g., Python, C++, Java) and familiarity with industry-standard coding practices.

 
 ML Frameworks & Advanced Optimization: Hands-on experience with PyTorch and other machine learning libraries (e.g., Scikit-Learn, TensorFlow). Deep understanding of model optimization pipelines, including PyTorch to ONNX conversions, ONNX Runtime, and scaling attention mechanisms (e.g., Flash Attention ).

 
 Data Systems: Experience working with large-scale computing frameworks, data analysis systems, and relational/non-relational databases.


 Nice to Have's:

text:
Senior Backend Engineer, Payments
 We are an international broker. Our clients fund and withdraw through roughly 60 payment methods across Asia, Africa, LATAM and the Middle East.
 Payments is now a standalone function, and we are building the team around it.
 We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer who will own our connector layer and everything downstream of it: building a canonical adapter layer so that providers plug in rather than get built one by one, moving payment methods to server-to-server and embedded flows, and making transaction status reliable and observable across the estate.
 You will also be the payments function's technical counterpart to the orchestration platform team: the behaviour we need from the platform is specified here, argued here and reviewed here.
 Your responsibilities will be:
 
 Building and owning the connector and adapter layer, so that adding or replacing a provider becomes configuration and a thin adapter rather than a new integration each time

 Migrating payment methods from redirect flows to server-to-server and embedded flows where the provider supports it, and measuring the result

 Owning everything downstream of the orchestration layer: reconciliation, transaction status handling on our side, method configuration and payment flows into the client portal

 Making transaction status reliable end to end, through active status polling, idempotent processing and reconciliation

 Building observability over transaction status and provider performance across the estate

 Specifying the behaviour we need from the orchestration platform: transaction state machine, idempotency, polling, routing and cascading rules. You design it, argue for it and review what comes back

 Supporting integration work for our card programme

 Extending the same integration set to acquired entities as configuration rather than a new build each time


 What you'll need:
 
 5+ years in backend engineering, strong in TypeScript, Node.js, comfortable in relational databases

 Production experience with payment systems: authorisation, callbacks, refunds, reconciliation and retry behaviour

 Practical understanding of idempotency, asynchronous status handling, transaction state machines and designing for partial failure. This is the core of the role rather than a detail, and you will both build against it and specify it

 Experience integrating third-party APIs of uneven quality, including working directly with a provider's integration team to resolve what the documentation does not answer

 The ability to own a service rather than close tickets: architecture decisions, standards and root cause fixes

 English and Russian at a working communicative level


 Will be a significant plus:
 
 Exposure to .NET for work touching the client portal

 Experience with APM and local rails in Asia, Africa or LATAM rather than cards alone

 Experience with bank transfer rails, virtual accounts, QR-based methods, mobile money etc.

 Event-driven patterns in production: transactional outbox, idempotent consumers, sagas

 Background in brokerage, crypto payments, orchestration or another high-volume payments environment; on the provider side, at a PSP, gateway or payment company

 Active use of AI tooling in daily work

 Ability to work independently and make decisions without constant oversight

 Proactive mindset: willingness to propose improvements, fixes, new approaches


 What the first year looks like:
 In the first months you take over the integration codebase with a documented handover, strengthen transaction status handling, and ship your first server-to-server integration.
 By mid-year the adapter layer is in place, new providers go live against it rather than as one-off builds, and transaction status and provider performance are observable across the estate.
 In the second half the migration to server-to-server and embedded flows runs as a programme across methods, and the same integration set starts extending to our other entities. As the team grows, a Systems Analyst takes over instrumentation and verification while integration engineering stays with you.
 Recruitment process:
 HR interview, covering background, motivation and fit
 Technical interview on backend engineering and the payments domain
 Home task as a case from the real needs
 System design and problem-solving interview, covering integration design, failure handling and status modelling
 Final interview with senior stakeholders
 We offer:
 Fixed monthly compensation of [based on experience]
 Fully remote work within GMT to GMT+4, with no relocation required
 Ownership of the connector layer and everything downstream, with direct influence on what the orchestration platform becomes
 Engineering problems that are not CRUD: asynchronous status across dozens of providers, partial failure, and local payment rails in emerging markets
 Scope that grows with the business: a card programme, new entities and new payment products
 Corporate AI tooling as part of the working process

 Tech Stack:

 observability tooling
